widgets_values:
.: V2V Editing (replace a character in a target video) --- NOTE: TENDS TO LOOK BETTER ON SINGLE PASS. SEE OPTION ABOVE ---

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the girl whose motion comes from <Video 1> and whose appearance comes from <Picture 1>.
<Video 1> is the source video for the target video edit.

summary:
[video editing + reference generation] The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>. The girl's appearance is styled from <Picture 1>. Her motion, camera movement, background, and lighting from the video are preserved continuously from start to finish without deviation at any point.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): partially_preserved - the girl's face, body proportions, and skin tone from <Picture 1> are retained, and her motion, choreography, rhythm, and timing from <Video 1> are retained at every moment. 
<Video 1> (whole-video temporal structure, motion path, camera movement, background, lighting): fully_preserved - the girl's choreography, movement speed, gestures, body positions, camera framing, camera movement, background, and lighting from every frame of <Video 1> are preserved throughout the entire target video without deviation.

detailed_description:
The target video uses a naturalistic style matching the source footage, preserving its original lighting, color grading, and camera work.
[Shot 1] The camera follows <Subject 1>, the girl, as she exists in the same setting from <Video 1>. Her appearance matches <Picture 1> — same skin tone, body shape, and natural contours. Throughout the entire video, her motion is a frame-by-frame motion match to <Video 1>: the same choreography, gestures, limb positions, movement speed, and rhythm are followed continuously from start to finish. The camera framing, angle, and movement stay locked to <Video 1> at all times. The background remains identical and unchanged.


.: Reference Generation (general filmmaking):

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the character in <Picture 1>. (basic description)

<Subject 2> is the scene location in <Picture 2>. (basic scene description)

summary:
[reference generation + audio reference] highly realistic live-action scene of <Subject 1> in <Subject 2>.

retention_analysis:
<Audio 1>: reference - its vocal timbre guides the vocal delivery of <Subject 1> without copying the original signal.

detailed_description:
[Shot 1]: a close up shot of <Subject 1> with a shocked expression as the camera pulls in towards her face. Suddenly, she turns around to look behind her.
[Shot 2]: a 3/4ths shot of <Subject 1> as she turns, her expression is confused. She tilts her head to one side, a look of questioning. She hesitantly says using <Audio 1> as her vocal-timbre reference: <d>[English]Hello?.. Is anyone there?</d> her tone is hesitant and suspicious.
[Shot 3]: an over-the-shoulder following shot as <Subject 1> begins to walk through <Subject 2> looking around side to side.
 
overall_soundscape:
interior ambience.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A

# MiniMax H3 Workflow Refactor

> **Design philosophy:** The user should control meaningful settings, while the workflow handles the internal routing, dependencies, and consequences automatically.

---

## Instructions

### 1. Prepare the Load Nodes

Disable any load nodes you're not using. Load media into every node you are using.

### 2. Configure the Control Panel

Use the **Control Panel** for the main workflow settings.

Set:

- Resolution
- Duration
- Reference counts
- Reference toggles
- Video Continuation
- Force Audio
- Final Upscale
- Interpolation
- Sparse Attention / VRAM options
- Sampler-related options

The workflow will handle the internal routing automatically based on those controls.

### 3. Configure References

Enable the references you want to use from the **Control Panel**.

You do not need to manually bypass individual reference groups.

Load the media you want to use into the corresponding:

- `<Picture>` reference nodes
- `<Audio>` reference nodes
- `<Video>` reference nodes

Only the references enabled by the controls are used for generation.

### 4. Set Video Reference Resolution Limits

When using a **video reference**, set the **Width** and **Height** values in the corresponding **Load Video** node to the maximum dimensions you want the reference video to use.

For example:

```text
Width: 768
Height: 768
Maintain Aspect Ratio: Selected

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the adult woman in <Picture 1>. Preserve her face, body shape, hairstyle, makeup, clothing, colors, and accessories as shown in the reference.
<Subject 2> is the environment in <Picture 2>. Preserve its visible layout, furnishings, materials, and colors.
<Audio 1> is the supplied singing audio for <Subject 1> (S1). Reuse its opening 5.00-second excerpt, preserving the actual singing, lyrics, original language, and accompaniment. She sings to the music of <Audio 1>, with her mouth movements synchronized to its sung vocals.

summary:
[reference generation + audio reuse] An 5.00-second realistic video shows <Subject 1> standing still with her right hand raised, and singing in <Subject 2>, the environment from <Picture 2>. Only her mouth and jaw move for the singing; her pose and the camera remain still throughout.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - preserve her referenced appearance while animating only the mouth and jaw movements necessary for singing.
<Subject 2> (throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - retain the environment from <Picture 2>.
<Audio 1>: partially_copy - directly reuse the opening 5.00-second singing excerpt as the soundtrack, with no added sounds.

detailed_description:
Realistic live-action cinematography. The duration is 5.00 seconds in one static shot she holding up ten fingers.

[Shot 1] A steady, eye-level medium-wide view shows <Subject 1> (S1), the adult woman from <Picture 1>, standing in <Subject 2>, the environment from <Picture 2>. Preserve her facial identity, body shape, hair, makeup, clothing, and accessories. Place her naturally within the setting, retaining its recognizable layout. She is holding her hand up nine fingers and lifts another holding up five fingers on one hand and five fingers on the other. She maintains this pose holding up ten fingers for the remainder of the video.

From 00:00.000 to 00:05.000, she sings to the music of <Audio 1>, following its actual vocal content, with lip and jaw movements precisely synchronized to the reused recording. Her voice, phrasing, emotion, and timing follow the supplied performance. Her head, torso, arms, hands, legs, and feet hold the same position throughout. Her gaze and facial expression remain steady apart from the movements needed to form the sung sounds. Her hair, clothing, and accessories stay still. Hold the camera at the same position, angle, and focal length for the entire video, maintaining the opening composition through the final frame.

nodes.title: Continuation mode: ON = REFRESHING (fresh gen + resample head), OFF = CLASSIC (guide + flat blend)
Guide (ON = no guide / refreshing, OFF = classic continuation guide)
Continuation mode switch
widgets_values:
**Continuation mode** (one boolean drives the guide switch and the head switch)

**OFF = classic:** `Guide for 1st Pass` conditions the generation on the uploaded clip's last N frames; the flat 0.5 `ImageBlend` joins the overlap.

**ON = refreshing:**
1. Fresh generation from your guides and prompt (no continuation guide).
2. The previous clip's last N frames are overlaid on the fresh gen's first N frames (old weight 1 -> 0 across the overlap), encoded, noised to HALF strength and denoised again (denoise 0.5), between two single-frame pins: the previous clip's first tail frame pins the START and the fresh gen's last overlap frame pins the END. The overlay carries the motion hand-over; the half-strength denoise merges the two takes into one. No mask, no taper, no hold.
3. Output = regenerated head + the rest of the fresh gen.

Two sampler passes run in this mode. If the resample does not run, check that the head switch is not bypassed.

**Landing guide** (inside the Refreshing group): a second guide pins the END of the resample window to the fresh gen's last overlap frame (same node, `frame_idx` -1, like the First and Last Frame subgraph). Switch it OFF to compare.

**Border in the second pass:** the same 50% horseshoe is applied to the resample pass as a latent noise mask on the overlay, so the top and side edges of the head stay closer to the overlay (framing stays put) while the rest is denoised.

nodes.title: Bottom % left OUT of the edge mask
top region: ones (W x region height)
PICTURE 2 BRANCH: crop + resize to generation size
duplicate Picture 2 frames for the duration
latent noise mask: 1 = regenerate, 0 = keep Picture 2
Picture 2 edge lock: how it works
widgets_values:
Branch from `<Picture 2>`: crop+resize to the generation size, duplicate it for `duration` frames, VAE-encode it as the sampler's starting latent.

Mask: everything is regenerated EXCEPT a horseshoe (edge px wide) along the left, top and right edges of the top region; the bottom % is fully regenerated. The horseshoe is multiplied by the `BORDER OPACITY` value (0.5 = the edge is kept 50% / regenerated 50%) and it stays on every frame; nothing shrinks or fades.

The mask goes through `MVEx_MaskToLatentSpace`, is inverted into a latent noise mask (1 = regenerate), and feeds the sampler. Bypass this group to restore the normal fresh latent.

**Moved:** the nodes that build the horseshoe (edge px, bottom %, border opacity) now live in the 'Border mask (shared)' group, because the resample pass uses the same mask.

nodes.title: Initial generation (no previous clip)
widgets_values:
**To generate the first clip:** in the yellow bypass panel, switch OFF **Seamless Continuation** and **Refreshing mode** (they go together; the second only works with the first).

**Picture 2 edge lock** is not in that panel (different colour), so it stays ON. It needs only Picture 2, width, height and duration.

Bypass its group directly if you ever want the plain fresh latent.

nodes.title: BORDER OPACITY: 0.5 = border kept at 50% (edit this value)
RESAMPLE: concat overlay latent (with border noise mask) + audio
Mode: head (ON = resampled head / refreshing, OFF = flat 0.5 blend / classic)
RESAMPLE: landing frame = fresh gen's last overlap frame
Landing guide: ON = also pin the end of the overlap, OFF = start guide only
RESAMPLE: START frame = previous clip's first tail frame
CROSSFADE weight of the OLD clip: 1.0 -> 0.0 (end index = Overlap Frames - 1 = 38)
OVERLAY: previous clip's tail over the fresh gen's head (old weight 1 -> 0)
PARTIAL DENOISE: denoise 0.5 (keep steps = 8 x denoise)
RESAMPLE border: duplicate for the overlap frames
RESAMPLE border: MVEx mask to latent space
RESAMPLE border: invert -> noise mask (1 = regenerate, 0.5 = border)
RESAMPLE border: SET LATENT NOISE MASK -> second sampler
